turns.t: It's the shoulder pain again, doctor. Eased off for a couple of weeks, then crept back.
Come in, sit down. So it settled for a while after last time, and now it's returned. Tell me what it's doing.
Aching, deep inside. Worse at night, lying on it.
That sounds miserable, your sleep must be suffering. Where exactly would you point to?
Here. Top of the arm, at the front, a bit round the back.
Thank you. Is it the pain that bothers you most, or more the way the shoulder moves?
Stiffness too. In the mornings. Takes an hour to loosen.
An hour, I see. And how would you rate the stiffness, mild, moderate, or worse than that?
Moderate. Getting dressed is the worst bit.
Mm. Getting dressed is a good test, because it needs reaching behind and overhead, which a stiff shoulder hates.
Yes. Pulling a jumper over my head.
Right. And what are you taking for it at the moment?
Paracetamol. When it's bad.
Is that helping, or just taking the edge off?
Edge off. That's all.
Fair enough. Any allergies to medicines I should know about, before we talk about anything else?
None.
Good. And the rest of you, any trouble with your breathing at the moment?
Fine.
Lovely. Now let me look at the shoulder. Lift your arm out to the side for me, slowly, and stop when it hurts.
Okay. Ow. That's as far as it goes.
Your shoulder movement is limited, it stops about halfway and the joint feels tight when I move it for you.
Is that bad?
Not bad as such, but I can't rule out a frozen shoulder at this stage. Picture the joint capsule like a jumper that shrank in the wash.
Right. How long does that take to go?
It can take months, I'm afraid, but most people get back to normal movement in the end.
Months. Okay.
Meanwhile, keep it moving. Gentle pendulum swings with the arm hanging down, a few minutes each day, and sleep on your other side hugging a pillow.
I can do that.
I'd like to see you again in six weeks, to check how much it has loosened.
Alright. Six weeks.
The receptionist will book that for you on your way out. Have you got any questions for me?
No. Thanks, doctor.
Take care, and be kind to that shoulder.
Will do. Bye.

clinical_actions.description: Keep shoulder moving with gentle pendulum exercises and sleep on the other side
